quote: You're right. Your bill isn't extremely high.
stewart_read: Customer's low-bill objection is the exact trigger for a flip (bill going to utility for decades vs solar), but rep validates it instead.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the shade genuinely disqualifying and used the bill comment as a soft landing rather than a real objection response.
coaching_implication: Coach the flip: even a $76-81 bill over 20+ years is money to the utility; rep should reframe before conceding the math.

quote: I mean, I'm more willing to listen.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a green light to keep going and the rep does not pick it up at all before disqualifying him two lines later.
coaching_implication: This is the single highest-leverage line in the call — rep should have asked a curiosity question ('what if the numbers still worked even with the tree?') instead of moving to removal.

quote: I can just remove you from my list.
stewart_read: Rep self-disqualifies on shading without confirming with a design/closer whether partial shade from one tree is a hard blocker, effectively making a closer-tier decision at setter stage.
alternative_hypothesis: Shade DQ could be a legitimate hard gate at Ion if severe enough, making this correct procedure rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Setter should not unilaterally DQ on shading judgment call — bridge to 'let our design team see if it still works' rather than removing from the list.

quote: one thing I'm a little concerned about is you've got some trees that are putting some shade on the home.
stewart_read: Rep makes a technical shading viability judgment (closer/design-tier content) at the setter stage instead of just capturing the roof/tree info and letting design assess.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be legitimate verify-section rapport if followed by continued qualification rather than a DQ — but the call shows it led directly to disqualification.
coaching_implication: Rep should note tree presence and move on, letting the design team make the shading call rather than voicing concern that primes the customer to defend the tree.

quote: the highest bill I've ever had was a $109.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a full bill history (highest and average) unprompted — a rich anchor point the rep never reflects back or uses.
coaching_implication: Rep should have used this detail as a hook ('so even at your lowest, that's still $75+/month going to the utility forever') instead of letting it sit as raw data.

stewart_read: Neutral/flat customer greeting is not acknowledged or warmed up before the rep launches straight into qualification questions.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's fast pace may be an intentional efficiency choice for a short call rather than a rapport miss.
coaching_implication: A brief warm acknowledgment before diving into address confirmation could soften the guarded start.
